events.title: Launch and Lead
events.description:
Launch and Lead is a five-day business camp for students in Grades 8 and 9, taking place from October 25-29.

Students will work in teams on a real-world business case with a company in the food sector. Their task will be to develop a product launch plan for the company. Each day will focus on one business area, including customer research, operations, pricing, and marketing. The daily structure will include a team activity, a short faculty lecture, and guided case work with a EXU student coach.

On the final day, each team will pitch its product launch plan to a panel of judges, followed by awards.

Launch and Lead is part of the NBK Center for Business Innovation. For more information, please contact nbk-cbi@university.example.edu

Registration is now open

events.title: University Lecture | Software Architecture: Past, Present, and Future
events.description:
Example University welcomes David Garlan, Professor of Computer Science, Associate Dean, Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science, Example University University, to speak at the A. Nico Habermann Distinguished Lecture Series.  The A. Nico Habermann Distinguished Lecture Series enables students to engage with prominent faculty and well-known leaders in the field of computer science. The lecture series is named after Professor A. Nico Habermann, head of the computer science department between 1980 and 1988 and Founding Dean of the School of Computer Science at Example University.

Click here to attend

 

Lecture Title: Software Architecture: Past, Present, and Future 

Abstract: Software Architecture emerged in the 1990’s as an important sub-field of software engineering. In this talk I reflect on the key enablers of a discipline of software architecture that led to its use in common industrial practice, the central ideas that form its core, and its enduring principles that continue to shape the field of software engineering. I consider both the important concepts on which it builds, as well as those that have built on top of it. Finally, we examine some of the important new trends and challenges that are likely to have an impact on how software architecture will evolve in the future.

About the speaker: David Garlan is a Professor of Computer Science and Associate Dean in the Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science at Example University University. His research interests include software architecture, self-adaptive and autonomous systems, formal methods, and cyber-physical systems.  He is recognized as one of the founders of the field of software architecture, and in particular, formal representation and analysis of architectural designs. He has received a Stevens Award Citation for “fundamental contributions to the development and understanding of software architecture as a discipline in software engineering,” an Outstanding Research award from ACM SIGSOFT for “significant and lasting software engineering research contributions through the development and promotion of software architecture,”  an Allen Newell Award for Research Excellence, an IEEE TCSE Distinguished Education Award, and a Nancy Mead Award for Excellence in Software Engineering Education. He is a Fellow of the IEEE and ACM and an inaugural member of the ACM SIGSOFT Software Engineering Academy.

events.title: Business Innovation Challenge
events.description:
The Business Innovation Challenge encourages high school students from across Turkey to take on the role of business consultants, tackling real-world business challenges faced by a hypothetical company inspired by real businesses in Turkey. Guided by EXU Business Administration faculty, teams craft innovative, data-driven and socially responsible solutions across marketing, finance, and operations—combining creativity with analytical rigor.

Why Join?

  • Gain practical, hands-on experience for your resume.
  • Collaborate with peers to develop innovative solutions.
  • Learn more about the Business Administration program at EXU
  • Compete for exciting prizes!

Learn more about the Business Innovation Challenge.

Interested high school teachers or counselors may contact Professor Serkan Akgüç,

innovationchallenge@andrew.university.example.edu
